subject: RFI: Commercial safeguards, smoothing and overage mechanics
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@alphafin.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Clarification on commercial section (smoothing / overage math)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the RFP docs — we're doing a line-by-line pass on commercial and had a few clarifying questions before we put the section into our procurement system: 

1) Smoothing/seasonality: can Redwood apply a 3-month smoothing window for commit coverage (i.e., deficits in month 1 can be pulled from month 2/3) and how is that reflected in overage invoicing?

2) Overage calculation: do overages bill on 'actual tokens' or 'billable units' after rounding/batching? Please provide an example calculation for spikes.

3) Price protection & model upgrades: if Redwood upgrades the underlying model or changes quantization, will AlphaFin receive a price protection guarantee for 12 months post-migration, or will the new model default to new pricing?

4) Caps/credits: does Redwood offer any cap on monthly overage for the first contract year or a breakage credit mechanism if commitments are materially underused?

We want to capture these items in our commercial terms. Can you send a short write-up or an exhibit we can attach to the RFP answer by EOD Monday?

—Alex
Alex Chen

Subject: RE: RFI: Clarification on commercial section (smoothing / overage math)

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. Attached are two artifacts: (1) Redwood_Pricing_Exhibit_v1.xlsx (line-item pricing examples and tier math) and (2) RDW_Commercial_QA.pdf (narrative answers & examples). Below is a concise summary you can paste into the RFP response.

Short answers (summary):
- Smoothing: We support a 3-month smoothing window by default. Deficits in month N may be offset by surplus in months N+1 and N+2; any net deficit after the 3-month window is invoiced as overage. Invoice timing: overages are invoiced monthly but marked as 'smoothed' in the exhibit; final true-up occurs at quarter close if requested.

- Overage calculation: Billable units = actual generated tokens (input+output) after internal batching; we bill on a per-token basis with rounding to the nearest 100 token bucket for invoicing efficiency. Example: if actual tokens = 123,450 in a month and rounding/bucket leaves 123,500 billable tokens, overage = max(0, billable_tokens - committed_tokens_for_month) * token_rate. See sheet tab 'Examples'.

- Price protection & model upgrades: For customers who subscribe to a 12+ month committed contract, Redwood offers a 12-month price protection window on materially equivalent model upgrades (same family / compute profile). If a customer elects to move to a higher-capability model, the parties can agree to a transition price; otherwise, new models carry their published rates.

- Caps/credits: For the initial contract year we can offer a monthly overage cap equal to 50% of the committed monthly token volume (i.e., cap = 0.5 * monthly_commit) to limit invoice shock. Additionally, we offer a quarterly breakage credit calculation: unused commits aggregated over the quarter may be converted to a credit at 25% of the unused value, applied to the following quarter's invoice (not refundable).

Proposed RFP exhibit language (short):
"Redwood Inference offers per-token billing with optional committed volumes and smoothing. Customers on 12+ month committed agreements receive a standard 3-month smoothing window, 12-month price protection on materially equivalent model upgrades, and a first-year monthly overage cap of 50% of committed monthly volume. Overage invoicing rounds billable tokens to 100-token buckets; overages are charged at the contracted token rate and are true-up eligible at quarter close. Unused commit credits may be applied to subsequent quarters at a 25% conversion rate. Additional commercial variations (higher caps, deeper credits) available by mutual agreement."

Next steps: I've cc'd Marissa (AE) — if you want, we can schedule a 30-min call Monday to lock final exhibit language and numbers. I've attached the two files; let me know if you need a version with line-item USD examples.

Thanks,

Folks — forwarding AlphaFin's questions and my draft exhibit (attached). Key asks for pricing approval:

- First-year concession: can we approve a 15% introductory discount on token rates for the first 12 months if they commit to a 12-month upfront minimum (annualized commit)?
- Smoothing + cap: recommend we accept the standard 3-month smoothing and 50% monthly overage cap for year 1; this limits exposure while staying competitive.
- Breakage credit: 25% conversion of unused commit to next-quarter credit — do finance/legal need specific language?

My recommendation: approve discount and smoothing/cap as proposed and let legal tighten the credit language. If approved, I will send a final commercial exhibit and DocuSign link.

Alex / Procurement team — thanks for the patience. Based on internal approvals, Redwood can confirm the following commercial terms for inclusion in the RFP response and subsequent contract: 

1) Commit & pricing: 12-month committed agreement (annualized) with the following illustrative price band:
   - Tier 1 (0 - 250M tokens/mo committed): $0.0009 / token (15% applied discount for first 12 months)
   - Tier 2 (250M - 1B tokens/mo): $0.00072 / token
   - Tier 3 (1B+ tokens/mo): custom enterprise pricing (contact AE)

2) Smoothing and true-up: Redwood supports a 3-month smoothing window. Overages are invoiced monthly using billable tokens rounded to 100-token buckets with a quarterly true-up option to reconcile smoothing adjustments.

3) Overage cap & credits: For contract year 1 Redwood will cap monthly overage invoiced to no more than 50% of the customer's committed monthly volume. Unused commit aggregated across a quarter may be converted to a credit applied to the following quarter at a 25% conversion rate.

4) Price protection & model upgrades: Redwood provides a 12-month price protection window on materially equivalent model upgrades for customers on 12+ month committed agreements. If AlphaFin opts into an upgraded, materially higher-capability model, the parties will negotiate transition pricing; absent agreement, new model rates will apply.

5) SLA and billing cadence: Standard invoice cadence is monthly with net-30 payment terms; SLA credits (service availability) are available per the standard SLA schedule in the contract.

Attachments: Redwood_Commercial_Exhibit_v2.xlsx (includes worked USD examples and a sample invoice with smoothing applied). DocuSign link for an initial SOW/Exhibit is below — we can populate actual commit numbers post-RFP review.
